_about: Hand-entered lead, paid and context data per report month. Fill each null as the numbers arrive; null shows on the dashboard as 'awaiting', never as zero. Reach is computed from the posts, so it is not entered here. 'untagged' is the count at that stage with no source recorded: it is reported openly, not hidden.

context.text: Lead ads start; daily views jump from about 15K to 70–98K until 13 Oct.
Second burst of lead ads, to 26 Oct.
Meta stopped reporting Facebook reach; viewers replaces it.
Instagram replied to 10.5% of messages in October, with an average reply time of 1h 47m (Meta inbox insights). 9 of 27 people who messaged came through ads.

Leads Centre shows 533 October leads; the ads report shows 397 form leads, 71 pixel leads and 78 workshop registrations (546). The two don't reconcile yet, and none of the 533 is marked converted, qualified or lost.
Grade-band lead ads (Grades 3–5, Nursery–PP2) ran 27–28 Oct: ₹19,799 for 44 leads.

web.basis: Google Analytics 4, sessions by channel. Export has no date range on it; read as 1–31 Oct. Test and spam traffic removed.

brief.headline: Meta ads turned ₹50K into 468 admission enquiries. Google took ₹81.6K and we can't yet say what it bought. Replies to parents and organic reach are where we're losing ground.

money.label: Meta lead ads
money.note: The main lead reel brought 396 enquiries at ₹64 each. The 27–28 Oct grade-band ads cost ₹381–₹503 each.

money.label: Google Performance Max
money.note: Google counts 631 conversions, but nobody has confirmed what a conversion is (form, call or page visit). Can't yet say what this spend bought.

money.label: Boosts and traffic
money.note: Bought attention, not enquiries. The traffic campaign was set to get likes instead of website clicks.

money.label: Diwali workshop
money.note: Event sign-ups for November. Each family is a warm lead once they're on campus.

working.title: The main lead reel
working.body: One reel brought 396 of October's 468 Meta enquiries. It's the cheapest way we have to reach a new parent.

working.title: Tatva's own stories
working.body: The Pakaashala kitchen reel reached 10.9K people and brought 58 new followers, the best post of the month. Real campus stories beat designed posts.

working.title: Proud moments
working.body: The Principal's Times School feature and the Taekwondo gold reached far more people than an ordinary static post.

working.title: Instagram is growing
working.body: Instagram follows rose 60% on September, helped by the ads.

notWorking.title: Parents' messages wait
notWorking.body: On Instagram, about 1 in 10 messages got a reply, and the average wait was 1 hour 47 minutes. Each unanswered message is an enquiry we paid for.

notWorking.title: Grade-band ads cost too much
notWorking.body: The 27–28 Oct ads for Grades 3–5 and Nursery–PP2 spent ₹19.8K for 44 enquiries, 6–8× the main reel.

notWorking.title: Money spent on likes
notWorking.body: Boosts and a misconfigured traffic campaign bought profile visits and likes, with no enquiries attached.

notWorking.title: Organic reach slipped
notWorking.body: Unpaid posts reached 36.8K people. 6 of 16 planned posts didn't go out as planned: 3 were replaced by Tatva posts and 3 reels waited on footage.

notWorking.title: We can't see what happens after the form
notWorking.body: None of the Meta leads is marked contacted, visited or lost, so nobody can tell which spend leads to campus visits.

decisions.text: Reply to every Instagram and WhatsApp message within an hour, including weekends.
Pause the grade-band ads and move that money to the main lead reel until a new version beats ₹100 a lead.
Mark every lead's status (contacted, visit booked, lost) in Leads Centre or the P800 tracker.
Confirm what Google counts as a conversion, and switch on Search ads for 'CBSE school Kukatpally'.
Send reel footage by the due date; 3 planned reels missed October.
